last_analysis: I can't see any scores, so I can't say which trial is best. The only evidence is that all 9 trials trained without errors, and that r3c2 shows a small network can run about 365k steps within the time limit. The remaining choices therefore rest on reasoning about the task. A brick placement is exact only if every cell under its footprint tops out at the same layer and the target is missing a cell at that layer in every one of them. The r3c3 head keeps each footprint cell separate, so it can learn this rule directly; pooling over the footprint loses which cell is which. Fresh random designs make more samples (1 epoch) a plausible gain for generalising to unseen designs, and wider context helps with build order. In this last round I combine these likely-good parts in different ways, which raises the chance that one 2-seed score beats the starting architecture. I don't change anything that is risky for the checks or the time limit.
